{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows sustained negative sentiment (e.g., multiple 0.00 or negative values) and model overestimates.",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude by 5-10% if true outcome consistently exceeds model forecast in the last 5-7 days, especially after recent spikes.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if model forecast is > 10% above recent 15-day average, reduce by 10-15% unless sentiment indicates bullish momentum.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment shifts: if sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.50) after a downtrend, adjust upward by 5-8%.",
    "Cap forecast growth after 3 consecutive days of >70% increase — avoid overshoots in volatile regimes.",
    "If true outcome is consistently 5-10% below model forecast over 3+ consecutive days, apply a downward bias of 3-5% to next forecast.",
    "For sentiment history with alternating 0.00/0.50, model should not overreact to single-day spikes — use 3-day moving average smoothing.",
    "When true outcome is >75% above 15-day average, reduce forecast by 10-15% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.",
    "If model forecast is >70% above true outcome for 3+ days, apply a downward correction of 5-10% per day to prevent persistent overestimation.",
    "For sentiment history with 0.00/0.33/0.50 patterns, model should not overreact to single-day spikes — use 3-day moving average smoothing."
  ]
}
